# Results — Study 449 (Renko-Charts) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py).  One recipe — build the
**ATR-Renko** brick series (brick size = 1.0 × median ATR(14)) from daily closes, run a
**10/30 simple-MA crossover** (long when fast > slow, else flat) on the Renko brick series,
and pin it head-to-head against the **same crossover on raw closes** and against
**buy-and-hold** — across a six-ETF basket.  As-of **2026-05-31** (the last complete month;
the partial June bar is dropped); history back to 2005-01-03.  One execution lag (signal at
close of *t* earns *t+1*'s return); turnover one-way × NAV.*

## The honest test — Renko crossover vs raw crossover vs buy-and-hold (pooled, gross)

Equal-weight portfolio of the six single-name strategies; gross (cost = 0).

| Arm | Sharpe | HAC *t* | ann. return | ann. vol | max DD | exposure |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Renko-filtered crossover** | **0.683** | **+3.43** | +6.78% | 9.61% | -17.8% | 0.90 |
| Raw-close crossover (control) | 0.685 | +3.43 | +6.77% | 9.56% | -19.6% | 0.90 |
| Buy-and-hold | 0.713 | +3.73 | +12.75% | 16.82% | -46.3% | 1.00 |

- **The incremental Renko edge is delta Sharpe = -0.002** — the brick filter changes nothing
  the eye could see.  Renko vs buy-and-hold is **-0.030 Sharpe**: the trend follower (Renko or
  raw) *under*-performs simply owning the basket.
- The crossover's own *t* = +3.43 is **bull-market beta, not Renko alpha** — it is long ~90% of
  the time over a 21-year up-market, so it inherits the drift, then gives some back to whipsaws
  (which is why its Sharpe sits *below* buy-and-hold's +3.73).

## Per-instrument (10/30 crossover, ATR-brick = 1.0 × ATR14, gross)

| Ticker | Renko Sharpe | Renko HAC *t* | Raw Sharpe | BH Sharpe | delta (Renko-raw) | brick |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 0.627 | +3.07 | 0.624 | 0.645 | +0.003 | 1.77 |
| QQQ | 0.740 | +3.52 | 0.772 | 0.778 | -0.032 | 1.19 |
| DIA | 0.554 | +2.66 | 0.490 | 0.617 | +0.064 | 1.50 |
| IWM | 0.374 | +1.88 | 0.405 | 0.470 | -0.031 | 1.51 |
| EFA | 0.289 | +1.44 | 0.320 | 0.391 | -0.030 | 0.57 |
| GLD | 0.514 | +2.48 | 0.481 | 0.677 | +0.033 | 1.58 |

The Renko-minus-raw delta is **near zero and changes sign** across instruments (positive for
DIA/GLD/SPY, negative for QQQ/IWM/EFA) — the signature of noise, not a filtering edge.  And on
**every** instrument both crossovers trail buy-and-hold.

## The myth-check: "Renko filters noise → fewer trades, cleaner signal"

| Arm (SPY) | trades / year |
|---|--:|
| Renko-filtered crossover | 7.8 |
| Raw-close crossover | 7.8 |

Identical turnover.  The ATR-brick is roughly one daily ATR wide, so on a daily tape the brick
series tracks the close almost step-for-step — there is **no extra smoothing** for a 10/30
crossover to benefit from.  The folk promise of a quieter, lower-turnover signal does not
materialise on daily bars.

## Could you trade it? — cost sweep (pooled, Sharpe)

| round-trip cost | Renko Sharpe | Raw Sharpe | delta |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | 0.683 | 0.685 | -0.002 |
| 1.0 bps | 0.674 | 0.676 | -0.001 |
| 2.0 bps | 0.665 | 0.666 | -0.001 |
| 5.0 bps | 0.639 | 0.639 | +0.000 |
| 10.0 bps | 0.595 | 0.593 | +0.002 |

Costs erode both arms equally (low, identical turnover).  At high cost the Renko arm edges
*marginally* ahead (+0.002 at 10 bps — it occasionally collapses a same-day in-and-out into one
brick), but the difference is well inside noise and never makes the strategy worth choosing over
buy-and-hold.

## Return-permutation placebo — the Renko advantage is noise

Shuffle SPY's daily log-returns (destroying all serial structure), rebuild the price path, and
re-measure the Renko-minus-raw Sharpe delta.  Over 500 shuffles:

| Observed delta (Renko-raw Sharpe) | placebo *p*-value |
|---|--:|
| +0.0029 | **0.495** |

A *p* of ~0.50 is exactly a coin flip: the tiny Renko edge on the real tape is **statistically
indistinguishable from what reshuffled noise produces**.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's a trend to find

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) with planted AR(1) return-persistence,
the crossover's Sharpe rises with the planted trend — the engine *can* detect and harvest trend:

| Planted trend | Renko Sharpe | Raw Sharpe | BH Sharpe | delta (Renko-raw) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (i.i.d.) | 0.123 | 0.076 | 0.085 | +0.047 |
| 0.05 | 0.171 | 0.096 | 0.085 | +0.075 |
| 0.10 | 0.193 | 0.145 | 0.085 | +0.048 |
| 0.15 | 0.163 | 0.170 | 0.085 | -0.007 |

The crossover Sharpe climbs as persistence is planted (machinery proof).  Even *here* the
Renko-over-raw delta is small and non-monotone — Renko's noise-filtering helps a little when the
trend is faint and then washes out as the trend strengthens.  The real tape behaves like the
"no exploitable persistence beyond drift" regime.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.**  The incremental Renko-over-raw delta Sharpe is **-0.002** pooled and flips
  sign instrument-by-instrument; the return-permutation placebo gives *p* = **0.495** (a coin
  flip).  The crossover's headline *t* = +3.43 is bull-market beta — it sits *below*
  buy-and-hold's +3.73, so there is no Renko *alpha* on this tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.**  Even gross, the Renko filter adds nothing; turnover is identical to
  the raw crossover (~7.8 trades/yr) and both arms trail simply owning the basket.  No cost
  level, no instrument, makes Renko the better choice.
- **"Renko gives a cleaner, lower-noise trend signal"? — BUSTED.**  On daily bars the ATR-brick
  is ~one ATR wide, so the brick series tracks the close step-for-step: same turnover, same
  Sharpe, same drawdowns as the raw crossover.  The "noise filter" is a redraw of the same chart.
